perspective:
Cynthia Huber’s available information:

- Cynthia works at a community center as an evening-class teacher. Christina Gonzalez is her colleague and the marketing manager. They are not close and have had professional disagreements about programs and community engagement.
- In a staff meeting about upcoming semester marketing materials, Cynthia argued for prominently featuring traditional classes, calling them the backbone of past success. She heard Christina argue for showcasing dynamic, interactive sessions and innovation. Cynthia replied that traditional methods are proven and that shifting focus too much could alienate long-time attendees. Christina said it was about enhancing offerings and finding balance, not replacing what works. Cynthia remained unconvinced and said the marketing should play to their core audience’s values of structure and depth.
- Cynthia later saw positive feedback from Christina’s last innovative marketing campaign. She asked Christina what she had done differently. Christina told her she focused on interactive elements and social media to create conversation rather than just broadcast information. Cynthia said this was intriguing and that Christina had managed to capture both depth and flash. Christina said they could blend new and old approaches and learn from each other.
- Cynthia proposed a joint pilot project combining traditional lectures with interactive online sessions. Christina liked the idea. They agreed to outline specifics and implementation. Cynthia hoped it would enhance learning and draw a wider audience.
- After the pilot, Cynthia believed it was a hit and wanted to scale it up immediately. She told Christina she would organize resources and set up a schedule. Christina said she would coordinate with marketing to spread the word. Cynthia expressed excitement about the impact.
- After the blended methods were implemented successfully, Cynthia received overwhelmingly positive feedback. She prepared a presentation to showcase the project’s success and advocate expanding it to other centers. She discussed this with Christina, who offered help and said other centers could benefit. Cynthia said she was proud and that blending their methods was the right move.

Cynthia has access only to what she personally experienced, said, did, observed, or was told by Christina in these interactions.
